provenance_note: These bounds were PRE-REGISTERED BY ANOTHER SESSION and reached this one before any span encode had been run here. They are adopted verbatim rather than rewritten: bounds authored after hearing a prediction are not bounds. This session verified only that the axis is runnable (48-frame clips load for both scenes, paste-back MAE 0.000) before adopting them. Copied into outputs/bp31-ladder/ because outputs/bp33-span/** is owned by the session that wrote the brief.

bounds.quantity: BD-rate at 48 frames per scene, panorama-stream, N=2 scenes, av1 preset 10
bounds.excursion_low: Below -40%: check the anchor was given all 48 frames JOINTLY, via the joint/separate control in plans/BP31-findings.md §5.
bounds.excursion_high: Above +65%: the plate grew far more than the canvas measurement predicts, or quality decayed enough that the residual ate the saving.
bounds.asymmetry_warning: A negative BD-rate is the result this project has been looking for, which is exactly why it gets an extra check rather than a celebration. Before reporting any win, confirm joint/separate still reads below 1.0 and that quality came from delivered_frames, not RunResult.frames.

bounds.quantity: plate bytes, 48 frames vs 8 frames, static clip (alcaraz_highlights)
bounds.excursion: Above 1.60x: the median over a long span is not converging; check foreground exclusion.

bounds.quantity: plate bytes, 48 frames vs 8 frames, moving clip (federer_djokovic/scene_003)
bounds.excursion: Above 2.50x: the canvas is running toward MAX_CANVAS_SCALE and the pan has left the plate's usefulness behind.

bounds.quantity: anchor bytes per frame, 48 frames vs 8 frames
bounds.excursion: Outside: the anchor is being run per-chunk rather than over the whole span.

bounds.quantity: delivered Y-PSNR at frame 47 minus frame 0
bounds.excursion: Below -4 dB: the homography has drifted off the plate and the product is a reconstruction that visibly rots, which is a different product from a uniform one. A clip MEAN hides this, which is why it is measured against frame index.

scope_stated_in_advance.n: Two scenes of one video. This decides an operating point for the extraction campaign; it is not a claim.
scope_stated_in_advance.one_thing_moves: Span only, with scene count held at N=2. BP33 §5: span and scene count are both amortisation axes on the same fixed cost and one sweep will not separate them.
